question: Which Part of the Indian Constitution provides for Fundamental Rights?
solution:
The correct answer is **"Part III".**** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Fundamental Rights** in India enshrined in the **Part** **III (Composition 12- 32) of the Constitution of India** guarantee civil liberties similar that all Indians can lead their lives in peace and harmony as citizens of India.
 
• These rights are known as **"abecedarian" **as they're most essential for all- round development i.e., material, intellectual, moral and spiritual and defended by abecedarian law of the land i.e. constitution.
 
• 
 These **include individual rights** common to utmost liberal republic, similar as equivalency before law, **freedom of speech and expression**, **freedom** **of association** and **peaceful assembly**, **freedom to exercise religion,** and the** right to indigenous remedies for the protection of civil rights** by means of writs similar as habeas corpus.
 
 
• 
 Violations of these rights affect in corrections as specified in the Indian Penal Code, subject to discretion of the bar.​
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 The **Fundamental Rights** are defined as introductory mortal freedoms which every Indian citizen has the right to enjoy **for a proper and harmonious development of personality.**
 
 
• 
 These **rights** widely **apply to all citizens,** irrespective **of race, place of birth, religion, estate or coitus**.
 
 
• 
 They're **enforceable by the courts,** subject to certain restrictions.
 
 
• 
 The Rights have their origins in numerous sources, including England's Bill of Rights, the United States Bill of Rights and France's protestation of the Rights of Man.
 
 
• 
 The** **Fundamental Rights are:

 
 
• 
 **Right to equivalency**( Composition 14 – 18)
 
 
• **Right to freedom**( Composition 19 – 22)
 
• **Right against exploitation**( Composition 23 – 24)
 
• **Right to freedom of religion**( Composition 25 – 28)
 
• **Cultural and educational rights**( Composition 29 – 30)
 
• **Right to indigenous remedies**( Composition 32)
